We observe that <MATH_0001> is a profinite
topological group, see Fundamental Groups, Definition
<REF_0001>.
The left hand categories are defined in
Section <REF_0002>.
The notation used in the right hand categories is taken from
Fundamental Groups, Definition <REF_0003>
for sets and
Definition <REF_0004> for abelian groups.
This explains the notation.

<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
Assertion (1) follows from
Lemma <REF_0005>
and Fundamental Groups, Theorem <REF_0006>.
Parts (2) and (3) follow immediately from this by endowing the underlying
(sheaves of) sets with additional structure. For example, a finite
locally constant sheaf of abelian groups on <MATH_0002> is the same thing
as a finite locally constant sheaf of sets <MATH_0003>
together with a map <MATH_0004>
satisfying the usual axioms. The equivalence in (1) sends products
to products and hence sends <MATH_0005> to an addition on the corresponding
finite <MATH_0006>-set. Since <MATH_0007>-modules
are the same thing as <MATH_0008>-sets with a compatible
abelian group structure we obtain (2). Part (3) is proved in
exactly the same way.
